project: QORE-VLM Phase 9H answerability and generation diagnostic

baseline.code_revision: five-ideas-development after the audited Phase 9G result
baseline.equivalence_test: The baseline arm calls unchanged Generator.generate with the selected QORE K=5 list; diagnostic arms only add report-only prompt probes and never alter retrieval, selection, evaluator, labels, or production settings

core_invariants: Each question is retrieved and selected exactly once before diagnostic outputs exist.
All generation arms use the same pinned model, deterministic decoding, evaluator normalization, and question.
The support judge receives an internal candidate answer but emits only a categorical model signal.
The extractive arm varies prompt wording only and copies answer words from selected context.
Baseline F1 is used as a deterministic format signal; raw predictions never cross the compact boundary.
Probe outputs never feed back into retrieval, selection, generation settings, or labels.
The existing Generator, selector, evaluator, and stable answer matcher are not modified.
A fresh held-out validation slice is used and compact output contains no raw text.

interfaces.output_schema: scalar EM, F1, and generation time
invariants: Uses unchanged Generator identity and deterministic decoding.
Raw prediction remains outside compact exchange output.

interfaces.input_schema: question, selected passages, and internal gold candidate
invariants: Model signal is report-only and never treated as ground truth.
Judge reason and raw output remain outside compact exchange output.

interfaces.input_schema: compact baseline, copy, extractive, support signal, and F1 records
interfaces.output_schema: cohorts, arm summaries, hierarchical attribution, paired bootstrap, and report-only gate
invariants: Primary attribution is restricted to selected-hit baseline EM errors with successful copy control.
Conflicting support/extraction signals remain a distinct class.

plugins.hypothesis: The unchanged generation arm is the reference.
Copy control separates output capability from evidence-use failure.
plugins.output_schema: conditional copy EM, F1, and time

plugins.hypothesis: A model-level support judgment can distinguish missing entailment from answer-use failure.
plugins.input_schema: selected passages, question, and internal gold candidate
failure_signatures: judge output includes reasons or is parsed ambiguously

plugins.hypothesis: Explicit span extraction recovers failures caused by the answer-generation contract.
failure_signatures: extractive prompt adds gold text or changes evaluator

plugins.hypothesis: Positive baseline F1 with EM failure is a possible answer-form mismatch.
plugins.output_schema: deterministic format signal consumed by combiner
failure_signatures: raw prediction is required for classification

plugins.hypothesis: Residual failures can be separated into support, extraction, format, semantic, unresolved, and contradictory signals.
failure_signatures: model signal is treated as truth

composition.merge_rule: Retrieve/select once, run baseline, copy control only on selected-hit baseline EM failures, run support and extractive probes only after copy success, and aggregate compact scalars/categorical labels only.
interaction_ablations: baseline F1 signal versus support/extraction classes

validation.baseline_equivalence: Synthetic fixtures prove unchanged Generator forwarding and stable prompt/parser behavior.

reproducibility.dataset_identity: nq_open validation[800:850], Wiki-DPR psgs_w100.nq.compressed, nprobe=64, one Top-50 retrieval and one frozen QORE K=5 selection per question
reproducibility.environment: runner records Python executable/version, git revision, config SHA-256, plugin tree hash, resolved generator identity/config hash, retrieval/selection settings, and output paths

limitations: The support judge is a model signal, not an independent entailment ground truth.
The extractive arm is an oracle-style prompt diagnostic and cannot support a production claim by itself.
Positive F1 with EM failure is only a possible answer-form mismatch, not proof of metric error.
A 50-question slice and deterministic decoding cannot establish broad generalization.
Every gate outcome is report-only and leaves production code unchanged.
